reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item: each explains the release/2.14 trap, uses origin/develop as the base, protects long-lived branches, gives a dry run and uses correct --merged / push --delete / branch -d commands. B is slightly safer: it limits the sweep to feature/*, saves a SHA backup file before deleting remote branches, and shows concretely how each base choice would hit the two risky branches. A's hotfix check (origin/develop..origin/main) can report false positives in git-flow because of release merge commits on main, and its chained single paste stops part way if any push batch is rejected.
